q: In 1831, Joseph Henry and Michael Faraday independently discovered the methods of producing electric current from magnetic field.
e: True. One farad is one coulomb per volt, so practical capacitors are µF, nF or pF. The year 1831 belongs to this fact, not a nearby discovery date.

q: A current flows through a loop of wire whenever there is a change in the magnetic lines of force through the loop.
e: True. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. Is a change in the magnetic lines of force through the loop.

q: The phenomenon where a current flows through a loop of wire due to a changing magnetic field is called electromagnetic radiation.
e: False. The right claim is this: A current flows through a loop of wire whenever there is a change in the magnetic lines of force through the loop; this phenomenon is called electromagnetic induction. A changing magnetic flux through a loop produces an induced emf and, if the path is closed, an induced current. The printed line wrongly says the phenomenon where a current flows through a loop of wire due to a changing magnetic field is called electromagnetic radiation.

q: The electromotive force (emf) which causes the induced current to flow is called an induced emf.
e: True. A changing magnetic flux through a loop produces an induced emf and, if the path is closed, an induced current. Which causes the induced current to flow is called an induced emf.

q: The magnetic flux density or magnetic induction B is the number of magnetic lines of force passing parallelly through a unit area of material.
e: False. The right claim is this: The magnetic flux density or magnetic induction B is the number of magnetic lines of force passing perpendicularly through a unit area of material. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane. The printed line wrongly says the magnetic flux density or magnetic induction B is the number of magnetic lines of force passing parallelly through a unit area of material.

q: The SI unit of magnetic flux density is the weber (Wb).
e: False. The right claim is this: The SI unit of magnetic flux is the weber (Wb). Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane. The printed line wrongly says the SI unit of magnetic flux density is the weber (Wb).

q: In electromagnetism, the magnetic flux through a surface is the surface integral of the normal component of the magnetic field B over that surface.
e: True. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane. Of the normal component of the magnetic field B over that surface.

q: The SI unit of magnetic flux is the tesla (T).
e: False. The right claim is this: The SI unit of magnetic flux is the weber (Wb). Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane. The printed line wrongly says the SI unit of magnetic flux is the tesla (T).

q: Magnetic field strength and magnetic flux density are vector quantities whereas magnetic flux is a scalar quantity.
e: True. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane. Flux density are vector quantities whereas magnetic flux is a scalar quantity.
